note_en: 得 after a verb introduces how or to what degree something happens: 逼得太紧 "push too hard," 笑得特别开心 "laughed really happily," 吓得躲进了自己的房间 "was so scared he hid in his room." English uses an adverb or "so... that," but Chinese puts the description after the verb with 得. Don't confuse it with 地, which goes before the verb (坦白地说出了自己的担忧 "frankly told him her worries"); both are pronounced de.
